messages.author: 0cc91f41491ff09e
messages.subject: mirtCAT without "next" button
parts:
Hi Phil & all,

first thanks a lot for your great work. Seems like an awesome piece of software :-)
Setting up my first CAT, I wondered if it is possible to not use the "next" button to get to the next question, but to automatically get to the next question after answering the question. That is, by selecting a solution from a multiple choice item, you get directly forwarded to the next item?
Would be a great feature for speed testing!

Thanks in advance,

Daniel

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: mirtCAT without "next" button
parts:
Hi Daniel,

It's possible with some internal editing, but that seems rather dangerous to do, and would be harder to merge into the more flexible item response formats (e.g., such as text inputs, or pull-down menus). In a pull-down interface, it's easy to imagine the user mis-clicking by a few pixels, which introduces unwanted error in your CAT session. I would generally advice against this form then, but of course it's possible to make a fork of mirtCAT on Github to work this way if you are really interested in this type of interface. HTH. 

Phil

parts: Hi Daniel,

On Sat, Apr 14, 2018 at 4:20 AM, Daniel Sommerhoff <daniel.s...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Phil,

thanks a lot for the quick reply and the info. I agree with your concerns, but for speed testing purposes the time between answering and pressing the "next" button may be negative for the interpretation of the data.

Shouldn't this be roughly constant for each participant? I don't really see this as a major limitation (it's not like the experiment is a kind of Stroop test, where important measures are recorded in milliseconds. Most test items times are more macro, often around 10+ seconds, so this effect doesn't seem that important overall).

As a follow-up question: If I see it correctly, the time  

A (possibly noob) follow-up question would be, if the item_times given bei mirtCAT refers to the time from the appearance of the item to the time a person presses "next". Could this be (easily) changed to the time until the (first) answer is selected? Or is this type of "click-stream-data" not accessible via mirtCAT?

Currently, not accessible, though theoretically this is possible by having the selection of a category signify an "event". The event in mirtCAT is tracked via the click button, again for compatibility with texts inputs, check boxes, etc. This alternative event tracking would require a fork of the source code, and may require a non-trivial amount of extra work. 

Phil

Thanks

Daniel

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: mirtCAT without "next" button
parts:
Part of the problem has to do with this issue related to shiny: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/928#issuecomment-381721943. 

If this gets patched, it's easily possible to add a separate tracker for the inputs changing, which should address @Daniel's timing concern as well (while also giving some freedom regarding retaining the 'Next' button). 

Phil
